trial_court: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sadulshahar, District Sri Ganganagar (Cr. Case No.81A/2016)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Vaishakha D/o Sh. Hari Ram, Aged About 22 Years, B/c Bhookhar Jat
parties.respondent_defendant: 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp; 2. Monika @ Mohini W/o Sh. Dharamveer, B/c Jat

facts_of_case: Complaint filed by respondent No.2 - Monika @ Mohini against Vaishakha and others for offences under Sections 494 and 120-B IPC.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage is void if at the date of such marriage either party had a husband or wife living.
legal_principles.held: Section 17 says that any marriage between two Hindus solemnized after the commencement of this Act is void if at the date of such marriage either party had a husband or a wife living.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage must be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto.
legal_principles.held: So, for a Hindu marriage to be valid has to be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto.

legal_principles.principle: To prove a second marriage between two Hindus to prosecute them for the offence of bigamy, it shall be proved that the second marriage is also solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies.
legal_principles.held: As per the settled law, even to prove a second marriage between two Hindus to prosecute them for the offence of bigamy punishable under Section 494 IPC, it shall be proved that the second marriage is also solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage is void if two conditions are satisfied: the marriage is solemnized after the commencement of the Act, and at the date of such marriage, either party had a spouse living.
legal_principles.held: It is further held that the word 'solemnize' means, in connection with a marriage, 'to celebrate the marriage with proper ceremonies and in due form', according to the Shorter Oxford Dictionary.
cited_cases: Bhaurao Shankar Lokhande v. State of Maharashtra : 1965 AIR 1564, 1965 SCR (2) 837

outcome.final_order: The order dated 02.02.2016 passed by the trial court was set aside.
